meta.label: Meditation apps
meta.attribution: These are the ways people in the US, the UK and elsewhere learn to meditate: the big subscription apps (Headspace, Calm, Happier, Waking Up, Balance, Breethe), a large free-with-premium library (Insight Timer), free apps from nonprofits, universities and governments (Medito, Smiling Mind, the Healthy Minds Program, Plum Village, UCLA Mindful, the VA's Mindfulness Coach, Dharma Seed), a free minimal app (Oak), free web routes (the Palouse Mindfulness MBSR course and Tara Brach's guided meditations), and borrowing a book or audiobook from a library. Method: privacy comes from each app's Apple App Store privacy label (scored lowest where data is used to track you across other companies' apps, then where it is linked to you for advertising), cross-checked against its privacy policy where we could read it. Cost uses App Store in-app prices and the provider's own pages; free routes score 100. Accessibility counts languages, App Store-declared accessibility features, platforms, and free access for people who cannot pay. Transparency scores how clearly subscription and auto-renew terms, refunds and cancellation are stated, and whether there is any subscription at all; we searched for FTC or state enforcement over these apps' subscriptions and found none, which is noted rather than scored. We do not score the quality or teaching of the meditations, and a privacy label is the developer's own declaration. Simple Habit was left out because its app has not been updated since December 2024. Sources: the Apple App Store, the providers' own terms, privacy and pricing pages, the VA, UCLA Health, Libby and The Reading Agency. Not medical advice: meditation is not a treatment for a mental health condition, and some people find it unsettling. If you are in crisis, call or text 988 in the US, or in the UK call 111 or Samaritans on 116 123. Reviewed 2026-10. Dispute or correct any rating via Contribute.

criteria.label: Least data collected and no ad tracking
Cost to you (free routes score highest)
Languages, accessibility features and free access
Clear subscription, auto-renew and refund terms

products.name: Headspace
products.description: One of the two best-known meditation subscriptions: guided courses, sleepcasts and focus music, now bundled with an AI companion and optional coaching and therapy.

privacy.note: Headspace's App Store privacy label declares no data used to track you, but links health, purchase, coarse location, contact, search, identifier and usage data to you and uses some of it for its own advertising or marketing. Its privacy policy says it does not sell personal information for payment but uses it to personalize the advertisements you receive about Headspace on third-party platforms.

economical.note: The App Store listing gives subscription options of $12.99 a month or $69.99 a year in the US after a free trial, with a Headspace Plus tier at $94.99; there is no meaningful free tier beyond the trial and a few sample sessions.

accessibility.note: The App Store lists Headspace in English only and says 'The developer has not yet indicated which accessibility features this app supports'; student and family plans are offered.

transparency.note: Headspace's terms say 'Free Trials automatically convert to a paid annual or monthly subscription term' unless you cancel first, that subscriptions continue until cancelled, and that you have no right to a refund 'unless otherwise required by applicable law'; its App Store listing states the prices and the 24-hour cancellation window before renewal. No FTC or state enforcement over its subscriptions was found.

products.name: Calm
products.description: The other mainstream meditation and sleep subscription, best known for sleep stories read by famous voices, with daily meditations, music and courses.

privacy.note: Calm's App Store privacy label lists purchases, identifiers and usage data as used to track you across other companies' apps and websites, and lists third-party advertising among the purposes for linked data such as user ID, device ID and product interaction. Calm's own privacy and terms pages put up a bot check that our reader could not pass, so this rests on the App Store declaration.

economical.note: Calm's App Store listing says some programs and features 'are free forever' but most content needs Calm Premium, listed at $14.99 to $16.99 a month and $69.99 to $79.99 a year in the US.

accessibility.note: The App Store lists Calm in English and nine other languages (French, German, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Spanish and Traditional Chinese), but says the developer has not indicated which accessibility features it supports.

transparency.note: Calm's App Store listing explains that subscriptions automatically renew unless auto-renew is turned off at least 24 hours before the period ends and that any unused free trial is forfeited on purchase, but does not state prices in the description (they appear only in the in-app purchase list), and calm.com's terms page could not be read without passing a bot check. No FTC or state enforcement over its subscriptions was found.

products.name: Insight Timer
products.description: A huge free library of guided meditations and talks uploaded by thousands of independent teachers, with an optional paid membership for courses and offline listening.

privacy.note: Insight Timer's App Store label declares no data used to track you, but links contact details, coarse location, search and browsing history, identifiers and usage data to you and uses contact details for its own advertising or marketing. Its privacy policy (effective August 6, 2025) says it does not sell or share personal data for targeted advertising.

economical.note: The free library is large and usable without paying; the App Store listing gives the optional subscription as US$59.99 a year or US$9.99 a month, plus optional teacher donations from $1.99.

accessibility.note: The App Store lists Insight Timer in English and nine other languages (Dutch, French, German, Hindi, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian and Spanish); no accessibility features are declared.

transparency.note: The App Store listing states both prices, says the subscription automatically renews at the end of each term unless auto-renew is turned off at least 24 hours before the period ends, and that refunds are not given for unused portions; the free tier never expires.

links.label: Insight Timer on the App Store

products.name: Happier (formerly Ten Percent Happier)
products.description: The app built around Dan Harris's book 10% Happier, renamed Happier in 2024 when Harris left the company and kept the podcast. Practical, skeptic-friendly courses and meditations from well-known teachers.

privacy.note: Happier's App Store privacy label declares no data used to track you, but lists third-party advertising among the purposes for linked usage data, and links contact details, identifiers, coarse location, search history and health data to you.

economical.note: The App Store lists an annual membership at $99.99 and monthly plans from $9.99 to $14.99, after a free trial.

accessibility.note: The App Store lists the app in English only, with no accessibility features declared.

transparency.note: The App Store listing explains that monthly and yearly memberships auto-renew unless turned off 24 hours before the period ends and that refunds are not issued for unused time, but gives prices only in the in-app purchase list. Its own September 2024 announcement says the app was renamed and that Dan Harris was 'transitioning away from his broader role within the app' while keeping the podcast.

products.name: Waking Up
products.description: Sam Harris's meditation and philosophy app: a structured introductory course plus lessons and conversations on attention, the self and contemplative traditions.

privacy.note: Waking Up's App Store label declares no data used to track you and lists no advertising purposes; it links purchase history, coarse location, email, identifiers and usage data to you for analytics, personalization and app functions.

economical.note: The App Store lists $19.99 a month or $149.99 a year ($229.99 for a family plan), among the most expensive here, but Waking Up says 'We offer a free membership to anyone who can't afford Waking Up', no questions asked.

accessibility.note: Free scholarship access removes the cost barrier, but the App Store lists the app in English only, with no accessibility features declared.

transparency.note: Waking Up's site says all subscriptions 'are protected by our risk-free money-back guarantee' and offers a no-questions free membership to anyone who cannot pay; its App Store listing states the renewal terms and says to email support for a full refund.

links.label: Waking Up on the App Store

products.name: Balance
products.description: A meditation app that builds a personalized daily plan from your answers to short questions, from The Mind Company, which also makes a brain-training app.

privacy.note: Balance's App Store privacy label lists identifiers as used to track you across other companies' apps and websites, and links purchase, contact, identifier and usage data to you, including for its own advertising or marketing.

economical.note: The App Store listing says that after a free trial Balance costs $11.99 a month or $69.99 a year, with a one-off lifetime option of $399.99.

accessibility.note: The App Store lists Balance in English only with no accessibility features declared.

transparency.note: Balance's App Store listing states its prices, that the subscription renews automatically unless turned off at least 24 hours before the end of the term, that renewals cost the same, and offers a one-off lifetime purchase as an alternative to auto-renewal.

products.name: Breethe
products.description: A meditation and sleep app with guided sessions, sleep stories and talks, a usable free version and paid premium plans.

privacy.note: Breethe's App Store privacy label lists purchases, identifiers and usage data as used to track you across other companies' apps and websites, and links contact and purchase data to you for its own advertising or marketing.

economical.note: The App Store listing says a free version is available 'as long as you want', with premium at $14.99 a month, $89.99 a year or a $179.99 lifetime payment.

accessibility.note: The App Store lists Breethe in English and Spanish, with no accessibility features declared.

transparency.note: Breethe's App Store listing states that the monthly membership 'autorenews for USD $14.99 per month' and the yearly plan for $89.99, and offers a one-time lifetime payment instead.

products.name: Medito
products.description: A completely free, open-source meditation app from a Dutch nonprofit foundation: guided meditations, courses, sleep stories and breathing exercises with no paywall and no ads.

privacy.note: Medito's App Store privacy label lists identifiers as used to track you across other companies' apps and websites, which is unusual for a nonprofit; its privacy policy explains that it uses advertising-measurement services including Meta alongside Firebase and Google Analytics, and says it does not sell personal information. Other data is listed as not linked to you.

economical.note: Medito says its tools are free with 'No paywalls, no ads, no exceptions' and that there are 'No trials, no premium tier'; the App Store lists no in-app purchases.

accessibility.note: The App Store says Medito supports larger text, a dark interface and sufficient contrast; Medito says it reaches people in 190+ countries, though the listing is English-only.

transparency.note: Medito says it is 'A registered non-profit in the Netherlands', publishes its registration numbers, and that 'The code is public', with the app under the AGPL licence; there is no subscription to renew.

products.name: Smiling Mind
products.description: A free mindfulness and mental fitness app from an Australian not-for-profit, with programs for children, families, schools and adults.

privacy.note: Smiling Mind's App Store label declares no tracking and no advertising purposes; it links health data, name, user ID and usage data to you for analytics, personalization and app functions.

economical.note: Smiling Mind describes 'our free app' for families, and the App Store lists it as free with no in-app purchases.

accessibility.note: The App Store says Smiling Mind supports VoiceOver, larger text and a dark interface, and rates it 4+ for children; it is listed in English only.

transparency.note: Smiling Mind describes itself as 'a leading Australian not-for-profit' and the app has no subscription to renew.

links.label: Smiling Mind on the App Store

products.name: Healthy Minds Program
products.description: A free meditation and podcast-style training program built on research from Richard Davidson's Center for Healthy Minds at the University of Wisconsin-Madison.

privacy.note: The App Store label declares no tracking, but links contact details, identifiers, usage data and data the developer labels sensitive to you, and uses email for its own advertising or marketing.

economical.note: The App Store lists the Healthy Minds Program as free with no in-app purchases; it is funded by its developer and donations.

accessibility.note: The App Store lists the app in English only with no accessibility features declared, rated 9+.

transparency.note: The App Store listing says the program is backed by research from 'the team at Humin (formerly Healthy Minds Innovations)' and the Center for Healthy Minds at the University of Wisconsin-Madison, and its June 2026 update notes record the name change; there is no subscription to renew.

links.label: Healthy Minds Program on the App Store

products.name: Plum Village
products.brand: Plum Village (Centre for Applied Ethics Ltd)
products.description: The free app of Thich Nhat Hanh's Zen community: guided meditations, deep relaxations, a mindfulness bell and talks by the monks and nuns.

privacy.note: Plum Village's App Store label declares no tracking; only email, name and support messages are linked to you, while analytics and diagnostics are not linked to your identity.

economical.note: The App Store listing says the app is 'Free forever with no ads or in-app purchases'.

accessibility.note: The App Store lists Plum Village in English, French, German, Italian, Portuguese, Spanish and Vietnamese, with 15 guided meditations for children; no accessibility features are declared.

transparency.note: Plum Village calls it 'A free app with guided meditations, deep relaxations and other practices' offered by Thich Nhat Hanh and his monastic community, supported by donations; there is no subscription.

links.label: Plum Village on the App Store

products.name: UCLA Mindful
products.description: The free app from UCLA Health's mindfulness education center, with short guided meditations for beginners and for health conditions, and Spanish-language meditations on its site.

privacy.note: UCLA Mindful's App Store label lists only data not linked to your identity: a device ID and usage data used for analytics and for the developer's own advertising or marketing, plus diagnostics. UCLA Mindful's app FAQ says it respects your privacy and does not share your personal information.

economical.note: UCLA Mindful's FAQ says 'The UCLA Mindful app meditations are completely free'.

accessibility.note: UCLA Mindful offers the app on iOS and Android and a separate set of meditations in Spanish (UCLA Mindful en Espanol) on its website; the app itself is listed in English with no accessibility features declared.

transparency.note: A university health system's free app with no in-app purchases or subscription, from UCLA's mindfulness education center.

links.label: UCLA Mindful on the App Store

products.name: Mindfulness Coach
products.description: A free mindfulness training app from the VA: guided exercises, a progress assessment and reminders, open to anyone, not only veterans.

privacy.note: The App Store listing says 'Mindfulness Coach is free, doesn't take or share any of your personal information', and its privacy label lists only data not linked to your identity.

economical.note: The VA lists Mindfulness Coach as a free download in its VA App Store for iOS and Android, with 12 audio-guided exercises and more available for free download.

accessibility.note: The App Store says the app supports VoiceOver, larger text and differentiation without colour alone; it is English-only and links to crisis resources.

transparency.note: Government-made, free, with no in-app purchases or subscription.

links.label: Mindfulness Coach on the App Store

products.name: Dharma Seed
products.description: A nonprofit archive of thousands of free dharma talks and guided meditations from Insight meditation teachers, by website or app.

privacy.note: Dharma Seed's App Store label lists only usage and diagnostic data, not linked to your identity.

economical.note: The App Store listing says teachers offer talks 'with the kind intention of dana, or generosity' and that they are made available to anyone 'regardless of financial means'; donations go to teachers.

accessibility.note: Talks can be streamed or downloaded on the website and the app; the app is listed in English only, with no accessibility features declared.

transparency.note: Dharma Seed says it 'is a 501(c)(3) Non-profit organization' and licenses its content under Creative Commons; there is nothing to subscribe to.

links.label: Dharma Seed on the App Store

products.name: Oak
products.description: A minimal, free iPhone app for breathing exercises and silent, guided and mantra meditation, with no premium tier pushed at you.

privacy.note: Oak's App Store label links only contact information to you; health, identifier, usage and diagnostic data are listed as not linked to your identity, with no tracking or advertising purposes.

economical.note: The App Store lists Oak as free; the only in-app purchase listed is a mantra meditation course priced $0.00.

accessibility.note: Oak's site says it is available on iOS only, and the App Store lists it in English with no accessibility features declared.

transparency.note: No subscription or paid tier is listed on the App Store, so there are no renewal terms to watch.

products.name: Palouse Mindfulness (free online MBSR)
products.description: A free, self-paced online version of the eight-week Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction course, made by a certified MBSR instructor. A website, not an app.

economical.note: Palouse Mindfulness says 'This online Mindfulness-Based Stress Reduction (MBSR) course is 100% free', based on the program founded by Jon Kabat-Zinn.

accessibility.note: The course runs in a web browser, with versions in English, Chinese, Italian, Japanese, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish and Turkish, and the site says it has more than 8,000 graduates from 120 countries.

transparency.note: Free, donation-supported, with no account or subscription required.

products.name: Tara Brach guided meditations
products.description: Hundreds of free guided meditations and talks from psychologist and meditation teacher Tara Brach, on her website and podcast, offered on a donation basis.

privacy.note: Tara Brach's privacy policy says 'We do not sell, trade, or otherwise transfer to outside parties' your personal information, but that cookies help 'keep track of advertisements' and that non-personally identifiable visitor information may be provided to other parties for marketing; listening needs no account.

economical.note: Her site asks for 'a donation of any size' so that the talks and meditations can be offered freely; nothing is paywalled.

accessibility.note: Meditations are free to stream on the website and through her podcast, with a translations section; there is no dedicated accessibility statement.

transparency.note: Donation-based with no subscription to renew; new meditations are posted weekly with dates.

products.name: Library books and audiobooks
products.description: Borrow a meditation or mindfulness book or audiobook from a public library, in person or through a free library app such as Libby. No subscription, no tracking of your mood.

privacy.note: Libby's App Store label lists only crash data linked to you, with usage and performance data not linked to your identity and no tracking; a paper book borrowed in person collects nothing about your practice.

economical.note: Libby's help pages say 'Libby is completely free' with a library card: 'There are no subscription costs, no in-app purchases, and no late fees.'

accessibility.note: In England and Wales, Reading Well's mental health list, recommended by health experts, includes 'Mindfulness: A practical guide to finding peace in a frantic world' and is stocked in every library service, often as e-books and audiobooks; Libby is listed in 19 languages and supports VoiceOver and Voice Control.

transparency.note: A library loan has no subscription or auto-renewal; Libby returns digital titles automatically on their due dates.

links.label: Reading Well for mental health (The Reading Agency)
